C-WINDOWS-MENU-ACCELERATORS.Name: Windows/Linux menu-accelerator rescue: window-level keydown dispatch for the hidden-bar chords
C-WINDOWS-MENU-ACCELERATORS.ApprovalBasis: Owner directive in chat 2026-11-01 («чинить давай все») issued right after the live polygon diagnosis was presented (dead Ctrl+S/N + mode trio via real SendInput; FIX-2 phantom; ☰-click artifact). The scope menu (recommended: full rescue of all win-relevant menu chords) was presented and closed without an answer; per the house rule an unanswered decision menu is not a rejection, so the published recommendation applies. Merge, train admission and release stay owner-controlled gates; this approval covers authoring and implementation on a branch only.
C-WINDOWS-MENU-ACCELERATORS.Summary: On Windows/Linux the C-15 T-W1 hidden menu bar (hide_menu in main.rs setup) leaves every app-level menu accelerator dead: the accelerator table lives with the visible bar, so real user input cannot reach the commands. Polygon proof with real SendInput (cua hotkey, foregrounded window): Ctrl+Alt+S, Ctrl+Alt+\, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+N and Ctrl+S all do nothing — Ctrl+S leaves a dirty document unsaved (file mtime unchanged); only renderer-bound chords respond (Ctrl+\ sidebar in editor.vue, the Ctrl+=/-/0 zoom trio in app.vue). The fix extends the established app.vue window-capture pattern: a new renderer module registers a window-level capture keydown dispatcher, gated to non-macOS, mapping an audit table of 22 menu chords to the SAME command registry ids the native menu dispatches (menu-bridge lookup reuse — no new command ids, no Rust changes). The change also corrects the Windows acceptance protocol: the "FIX-2 mode chips do not render" finding is reclassified as a measurement phantom (the rounds' dispatcher ipcRenderer.invoke('mt::menu-invoked') is a silent v1-stub no-op and the loose selectors matched resting-state elements), with the strict selector, pinia-state assertion and working event-emit dispatch recipe landing in the protocol doc.
C-WINDOWS-MENU-ACCELERATORS.ProblemEvidence: 2026-11-01 polygon session (Mark NSIS from main 388b6669, live CDP + cua): (1) real SendInput Ctrl+Alt+S / Ctrl+Alt+\ / Ctrl+D / Ctrl+N / Ctrl+S to the foregrounded main window — no effect (pinia flags unmoved; dirty README.md not written, mtime 31.10 13:00 unchanged after Ctrl+S); (2) the same commands dispatched as the mt::menu-invoked event execute perfectly and the C-TITLEBAR-MODE-CHIPS chips render — chips 0 in the rounds was correct no-mode behavior, not a renderer bug; (3) trusted clicks DO reach the ☰ button (capture-phase pointerdown/mousedown/click on .titlebar-nav-menu, isTrusted=true) and the mt::window-popup-app-menu invoke opens the native menu — the rehearsal's "click does not reach" was a 125%-scale coordinate artifact; (4) renderer-bound chords are alive (Ctrl+\ sidebar, zoom trio), isolating the dead surface to menu accelerators specifically. Root cause: main.rs #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))] hide_menu() — muda processes menu accelerators through the visible menu bar; hidden bar = unregistered accelerators.

Goals.Goal: A new renderer module (src/renderer/src/services/windowMenuAccelerators.js) owns the rescue: a window-level capture keydown listener registered once at boot on non-macOS, a pure accelerator table mapping physical-key chords to existing command registry ids, and the same dispatch path the menu bridge uses — one table, one dispatcher, no per-component patches.

The table covers the audited 22 dead chords: Ctrl+N file.new-tab, Ctrl+O file.open-file, Ctrl+Shift+O file.add-folder, Alt+Ctrl+V file.open-from-clipboard, Ctrl+S file.save, Ctrl+Shift+S file.save-as, Ctrl+W file.close-tab, Ctrl+Shift+T file.reopen-closed-tab, Ctrl+P file.print, Ctrl+A edit.select-all, Ctrl+F edit.find, Ctrl+G edit.find-next, Ctrl+Shift+G edit.find-previous, Ctrl+H edit.replace, Ctrl+Shift+F edit.find-in-folder, Ctrl+B view.toggle-sidebar, Ctrl+Alt+S view.source-code-mode, Ctrl+Alt+\ view.split-view, Ctrl+D view.diff-mode, Ctrl+Tab tabs.cycleForward, Ctrl+Shift+Tab tabs.cycleBackward, Ctrl+M window.minimize — with IME-composition and auto-repeat guards, physical event.code matching for layout independence, and input-surface carve-outs where the browser default is the correct behavior (Ctrl+A inside non-editor inputs).

The Windows acceptance protocol (docs/acceptance/cua-e2e-windows-polygon.md) carries the FIX-2 errata and the corrected probe recipe: strict chip selector (.titlebar-mode-chips-wrap .mode-chip), pinia-state assertions for mode engagement, the working dispatch (Tauri event emit of mt::menu-invoked — never ipcRenderer.invoke), the real-input accelerator test via cua hotkey, and the 125% scale trap for coordinate math.

Constraints.Constraint: No global shortcuts: tauri-plugin-global-shortcut / M-006 registration is rejected for this surface — system-wide registration would steal Ctrl+S/N/F from other applications; menu-accelerator semantics are app-focused, and the window-level keydown dispatcher preserves exactly that.

macOS is untouched: the handler is gated off with isOsx (the native menu owns the chords there); chords already alive in the renderer are excluded from the table (zoom trio Ctrl+=/-/0 lives in app.vue setupZoomKeysFontSize; Ctrl+\ sidebar lives in editor.vue) so nothing double-fires.

No Rust changes and no m009_menu.rs changes: the native menu, its labels and its declared accelerators stay exactly as they are (the ☰ popup path works and keeps working); the rescue is additive renderer behavior for the surfaces the hidden bar cannot serve.

Dispatch parity only: the table maps to existing command ids resolved through the existing static command registry (menu-bridge's findCommandById reuse or equivalent import) — no new command ids, no new end states, no reordering of the exclusive view normalization.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No fullscreen chord rescue: the declared Ctrl+CmdOrCtrl+F is degenerate on Windows (double modifier) and full screen stays reachable via the ☰ menu; no F11 introduction.
No Command Palette on Windows/Linux: view.command-palette stays macOS-only per FIX-010 / UC-025.
No FIX-2 renderer work: mode chips are proven functional (probe evidence); no modeChips.vue changes ship in this change.
No live Linux verification (no Linux polygon exists): Linux rides the same !macOS gate and code path; CI/e2e cover the logic, the platform gap is documented.
No repair of the C-15 T-W1 hidden-bar decision itself: the custom titlebar keeps hiding the native bar; making muda register accelerators for a hidden bar is an upstream question, not ours.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Unit tests pin the table: every entry maps to a command id that exists in the static registry, the m009 cross-check test proves table parity with the win-relevant accelerators declared in m009_menu.rs (parsed from source, so drift breaks CI), the excluded-alive chords (zoom trio, mac-only trio, fullscreen) are asserted absent, and the macOS gate, IME guard, repeat guard and input-surface carve-outs are asserted.

E2E (chromium tauri-shim, platform stubbed win32): each representative chord dispatches its command through the window dispatcher — Ctrl+Alt+S turns sourceCode on AND renders the mode chip, Ctrl+S saves a dirty doc, Ctrl+W closes the focused tab — and the dispatcher stays silent on darwin-stubbed runs.

Polygon acceptance on the rebuilt NSIS: real cua hotkey Ctrl+Alt+S engages Source Code Mode with the titlebar chip rendering (the C-TITLEBAR-MODE-CHIPS Windows acceptance effect), Ctrl+S writes a dirty scratch doc (mtime moves), Ctrl+N opens a tab; the ☰ click path re-verified (menu opens from a real click at rect coordinates).

The protocol doc errata lands: FIX-2 reclassified with the phantom evidence, strict selectors + pinia assertions + event-emit dispatch + hotkey recipe + 125% scale trap replace the round recipe that produced the false reproduction.

AffectedAreas.Area: src/renderer/src/services/windowMenuAccelerators.js (new module + MODULE_CONTRACT/MAP); src/renderer/src/pages/app.vue (boot wiring beside the existing zoom/palette capture handlers + CHANGE_SUMMARY); src/renderer/src/menu-bridge.js (export findCommandById for reuse, contract note); tests/renderer/services/windowMenuAccelerators.test.js (new) + m009 parity cross-check; tests/e2e/windows-accelerators.spec.ts (new); docs/acceptance/cua-e2e-windows-polygon.md (errata + corrected recipe); .grace/graph + .grace/verification entries per plan; docs/release-trains/2.9.x-next.md train admission.

Assumptions.Assumption: WebView2 delivers Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab to the page (browser-level tab switching is not in play inside a Tauri webview); if the polygon run shows the chord swallowed, the two tab-cycle entries drop to a documented follow-up without touching the rest of the table.
Ctrl+P inside WebView2 does not open a browser print dialog before the page sees the keydown (preventDefault in the dispatcher covers it if it does).
The plugin:event|emit dispatch used by the acceptance recipe stays available to CDP probes (core:event:allow-emit already granted to the app itself).
